France mounts huge security operation as protesters prepare to march

Reuters

24 October, 2026 03:30 pm IST

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

By Crispian Balmer and Elizabeth Pineau PARIS, Oct 24 (Reuters) – French security forces fanned out across Paris on Saturday ahead of protests that authorities fear could turn violent, with Interior Minister Laurent Nunez urging police to be “hyper-reactive” against troublemakers and looters.

Soldiers from an anti-terrorism military unit patrolled the Champs-Elysees avenue while police vans circled the Arc de Triomphe, looking to protect some of the capital’s most famous sites from any repeat of the unrest that shook France last week.

Nunez has mobilised 70,000 police nationwide for Saturday’s demonstrations, 10,000 more than on October 17, when a wave of vandalism and looting raised questions about the government’s ability to maintain order.

Show Full Article

Anger over living costs and strained public services has drawn students, workers and unions onto the streets in recent weeks, but authorities say radical militants and bands of young looters have exploited the protests to sow chaos.

Speaking to police in Paris, Nunez warned officers that they would face attempts to target shops, public institutions and security forces.

“We have to be ultra, ultra responsive. We have significant calls for disruption from political groups and quite simply from criminals,” he said. “It is going to be a long day.”

SHOPS, MUSEUMS, OPERA SHUT

Many shopkeepers in Paris boarded up storefronts, while luxury retailers beefed up security.

Business groups have urged stores to remain closed after thousands of shops and businesses were damaged or looted across France last weekend.

Lidiya Shevchenko, a sales assistant at a Graziella Braccialini store in Paris, said she doubted many customers would venture out to browse luxury boutiques during the day.

“I suppose the mood is just as important when it comes to shopping,” she said.

Several of Paris’ best-known cultural institutions, including the Louvre, the Musée d’Orsay and the Opera House, will close for the day to avoid being caught up in any turmoil. More than 20 metro stations were also shut.

The location of Saturday’s main Paris demonstration remained unclear after police sought to move organisers away from the city centre towards the southeastern fringes of the capital.

“The declared route poses serious risks of disturbances to public order, notably because of the high concentration of businesses similar to those targeted during the weekend of October 17-18,” the Paris police prefecture said.

The last-minute decision angered some on the left.

“Once again, those in power are creating disruption for the marches and impossible deadlines for organisations to reorganise themselves. These methods are multiplying across the entire country,” hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon wrote on X.

DEMONSTRATION IN ORLEANS AGAINST FAR RIGHT

Authorities have sharply restricted demonstrations across much of France. Marseille reversed an earlier ban and authorised a union march, while protests remain restricted in central Lyon. Union rallies will also go ahead in Strasbourg, but bans remain in force in several other cities including Nancy, Metz, Besancon, Belfort, Rouen, Le Havre, Toulon and Limoges.

The first authorised march began mid-morning in Orleans, about 120 km (75 miles) south of Paris, to protest against Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally, which is holding a congress in the city this weekend.

“We have come to tell the far right, face to face, that we are not afraid,” said Bally Bagayoko, the mayor of Saint-Denis and a member of the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party.

Tensions were heightened by a shooting west of Paris on Friday in which a gunman suspected of acting out of Islamophobic hatred killed one person and wounded four others, including a 12-year-old girl.

(Reporting by Crispian Balmer, Bertrand Boucey, Alessandro Parodi in Paris and Elizabeth Pineau in Orleans. Editing by Mark Potter)

North Korea’s Kim Jong Un visits China via Dandong bridge, South Korean official says

Reuters

24 October, 2026 01:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Joyce Lee SEOUL, Oct 24 (Reuters) – North Korean leader Kim Jong Un arrived in China on Saturday, visiting the neighbouring country via a newly opened bridge, a South Korean government official said.

Kim arrived in Dandong through the New Yalu River Bridge connecting North Korea and China, the official said on condition of anonymity as they are not authorised to speak publicly about the matter.

Chinese Premier Li Qiang met Kim in the border city, South Korea’s Yonhap news agency said. Kim’s visit comes a day before the anniversary of China joining the 1950-1953 Korean War.

Show Full Article

China’s foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

China and North Korea opened the 3-km (2-mile) New Yalu River Bridge, their most significant land border crossing, this month after a long delay, aiming to rejuvenate trade and commerce after years of strained ties and pandemic-related disruptions.

A visit by Kim now is consistent with the current phase of closer economic ties and more frequent high-level exchanges between China and North Korea, said Lu Chao, an expert in China-North Korea relations at the Liaoning Academy of Social Sciences, a Chinese government think-tank in Shenyang.

“The opening of the bridge has resolved a major bottleneck in China-North Korea trade logistics,” Lu said. “With the logistics constraint eased, bilateral trade is likely to increase further.”

The bridge is expected to help move heavy equipment, raw materials and energy products that North Korea needs for development. The opening is the latest sign of warming ties between Beijing and Pyongyang, after two summits between their leaders in the past 13 months.

Kim’s last known visit to China was in September 2025, to attend the 80th Victory Day celebrations in Beijing, when he held a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Xi made a state visit to North Korea in June.

“It is too early to divine Kim’s intentions because he is only in Dandong,” said Christopher Green, a Korea specialist at Leiden University in the Netherlands. “Will there be a Xi-Kim summit? Probably — it would be surprising if there were not. However, nothing is certain at this stage.”

China, which fought alongside North Korea in the Korean War, is Pyongyang’s main economic and diplomatic backer and accounts for most of its official trade. However, North Korea has drawn closer to Russia since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, which analysts say has reduced Pyongyang’s reliance on Beijing.

US President Donald Trump has been eager to jump-start talks with North Korea, but US and South Korean officials see fading chances of him meeting Kim this year, Reuters reported on Friday.

China hosts a summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum next month in Shenzhen, which Trump is expected to attend.

(Reporting by Joyce Lee and Brenda Goh in Seoul, Eduardo Baptista in Beijing; Editing by William Mallard)
